paragraphs: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yitzchak. (A tanna cited in a baraita.)

In Kiddushin 54a, the baraita reads: “R. Y. son of R. Y. said: The stones of Jerusalem that fell are subject to me’ilah—the words of Rabbi Meir,” etc. Without doubt this is a copyist’s error, and it should read: “Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yitzchak recited the teaching.” In fact, he was an amora, a student of Rabbi Yochanan. In Yoma, chapter 3, halakhah 7: “Rabbi Yishmael son of Rav Yitzchak; Rabbi Yochanan in the name of Rabbi Shimon bar Yoḥai.”[^1][^2]

notes.text: Hyman prints אר״י בר״י, “R. Y. son of R. Y.” His proposed דתני, “recited the teaching,” makes Yishmael the transmitter of the baraita rather than its tanna. Me’ilah is the misuse of consecrated property.

Kiddushin 54a:6 in the William Davidson edition names Rabbi Yishmael bar Rabbi Yitzchak. The corresponding Jerusalem Talmud Yoma 3:7:4 passage in the Guggenheimer edition instead begins “Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak; Rabbi Yochanan in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai.” Hyman gives Yishmael, not Shmuel, and calls his father Rav Yitzchak in this citation.
